workload: One 1 MiB upload.GetFile chunk, the size Client.get_file requests, decrypted with AES-256-IGE.
notes: With no kuricrypt or tgcrypto installed, every MTProto payload is decrypted by ige, including each 1 MiB chunk Client.get_file asks upload.GetFile for. ige copies the chunk into a list of 16-byte bytes objects and keeps that list until b''.join. tracemalloc peak for one decrypt is 10072926 bytes; the seven samples span 56 bytes. A decrypt that writes blocks into one bytearray and returns that buffer peaks near 2.1 MiB on the same chunk, about 7.6 MiB lower, and returns the same plaintext. tests/unit/session/test_session.py calls ige256_encrypt and ige256_decrypt, which call ige on this fallback (14 calls in that run).

workload: The 131072 16-byte xors performed while AES-256-IGE decrypts one 1 MiB file chunk.
notes: ige calls xor twice per 16-byte block, so one 1 MiB upload.GetFile chunk is 131072 xors. xor builds each result with bytes(i ^ j for i, j in zip(...)), one Python int per byte. Timing only those calls takes 116.3299 ms (full spread 2.8015% over 7 samples). A length-checked word xor via int.from_bytes returns the same bytes for those 16-byte blocks and for empty, 1, 15, 32, and 256-byte inputs, and drops the same batch from about 115 ms to about 32 ms. Patched into ige256_decrypt, the chunk median moved from about 1715 ms to about 1674 ms. The session tests execute this path: 152 xor calls while test_session.py passes.
